strings.title: The Dawn Dose
strings.hint: Read what the victim planned to send that morning... then compare the insulin dispensing signatures with their supposed authors' genuine signatures.
strings.solvedText:
Culprit: charge nurse Ramez Helou.

For a year, he had been stealing narcotic medications from the ward's stock and covering the thefts with forged signatures. Dr. Bassel stumbled upon the trail while auditing an old death and prepared a formal report to send the morning of his shift. At dawn, Ramez entered the on-call room with his access card and injected the sleeping doctor, who was not diabetic, with a fatal dose of insulin, hoping the death would be recorded as a sudden collapse.

What convicted him: missing insulin signed out with a forged signature, his access-card record at the room's door at 04:10, and the victim's report, which arrived despite his death — he had scheduled it to send automatically.
strings.summary.text: Consultant physician Dr. Bassel Omran was found dead in the doctors' on-call room at sunrise. At first glance: a heart attack during sleep. But the forensic examiner noticed a fresh injection mark behind his shoulder. Tests revealed a massive insulin dose in the blood of a man who did not have diabetes. In a sleeping hospital, who can carry a syringe at four in the morning without attracting attention?
strings.summary.victim.name: Dr. Bassel Omran
strings.summary.victim.job: Consultant physician — chair of the medication audit committee
strings.summary.timeline[1].l: Entered the on-call room to sleep
strings.summary.timeline[2].l: Room opened with a staff access card
strings.scene.address: Al-Rahma Hospital — fourth floor, doctors' on-call room
strings.scene.intro: No struggle: the injection was delivered behind his left shoulder while he slept deeply. The killer knew where the insulin pens were stored, how to open the room, and when hospital oversight was lightest: four in the morning.
strings.scene.photos[0].cap: Injection site behind the shoulder — examination report
strings.scene.notes[0]: A fresh injection mark behind the left shoulder
strings.scene.notes[1]: A fatal insulin dose in a person without diabetes
strings.scene.notes[2]: The room was opened with a staff access card at 04:10
strings.scene.notes[3]: The victim had been auditing old medication dispensing records
strings.evidence[0].title: The Empty Insulin Pen
strings.evidence[0].desc: A pen from the ward's own stock batch. It had been wiped, but a nylon glove impression remained.
strings.evidence[1].title: Door Access-Card Log
strings.evidence[1].desc: The charge nurse's card opened the on-call room at 04:10 for two minutes, outside any recorded assignment.
strings.evidence[2].title: The Victim's Draft Report
strings.evidence[2].desc: A report to management about 'systematic medication shortages concealed by forged signatures' — sent automatically at 08:00 after his death.
strings.evidence[3].title: Insulin Stock Ledger
strings.evidence[3].desc: 3 pens missing this month, signed out for patients discharged before the recorded dates.
strings.evidence[4].title: The Former Patient's Lawsuit
strings.evidence[4].desc: A patient suing Dr. Bassel and openly threatening him in the corridors — a conspicuous early lead.
strings.evidence[5].title: Department Head Candidacy List
strings.evidence[5].desc: Dr. Bassel and his colleague were the only candidates for the vacant department head position.
strings.suspects[0].name: Ramez Helou
strings.suspects[0].alibi: 'My night rounds are documented — opening rooms is part of my job.'
strings.suspects[0].statement: I opened the on-call room at dawn to check the air conditioning after a complaint. I did not wake the doctor or go near him. As for the stock, mistakes happen in every ward. Audit anyone and you will find something.
strings.suspects[1].name: Dr. Hala Nassar
strings.suspects[1].alibi: 'I was in emergency surgery from three until six, with an entire team beside me.'
strings.suspects[1].statement: Our rivalry was fierce but academic: papers, conferences, committees. His death did not give me the position; it froze the appointment. The entire hospital is now under scrutiny that benefits nobody.
strings.suspects[2].name: Former patient Abu Walid
strings.suspects[2].alibi: 'I was asleep at home. Besides, an administrative order bans me from the hospital.'
strings.suspects[2].statement: I threatened him with courts, not injections. I cannot tell insulin from aspirin. His death wronged me twice: he died before apologizing and before I could win my case.
strings.witnesses[0].name: Nurse on duty
strings.witnesses[0].statement: I saw charge nurse Ramez leaving the on-call corridor at dawn with something pen-sized in his pocket. He put his hand over it when he noticed me.
strings.witnesses[1].name: Cleaner
strings.witnesses[1].statement: The second-floor bin was empty at midnight. In the morning, it contained a single injection pen. Who goes down two floors to throw away a pen?
strings.witnesses[2].name: Committee secretary
strings.witnesses[2].statement: The day before, Dr. Bassel requested 14 months of dispensing records for the west wing. He said: 'Numbers do not lie... the people signing do.'
strings.folders[0].name: Incident reports
strings.folders[0].docs[0].title: Death Notification
strings.folders[0].docs[0].body: Notification of a doctor's death in the on-call room. It became a criminal case after the injection mark was noticed.
strings.folders[1].name: Forensic evidence
strings.folders[1].docs[0].title: Toxicology report
strings.folders[1].docs[0].body: A fatal insulin dose in a person without diabetes. The injection time matches the 04:10 window.
strings.folders[1].docs[1].title: Pen Examination Report
strings.folders[1].docs[1].body: The pen came from the west wing's stock batch. Its nylon glove impression matches the type supplied in nursing glove boxes.
strings.folders[2].name: Interviews
strings.folders[2].docs[0].title: Charge Nurse Interview
strings.folders[2].docs[0].body: There is no air-conditioning complaint in the incident log. He became flustered when the pen in his pocket was mentioned.
strings.folders[2].docs[1].title: Dr. Hala Interview
strings.folders[2].docs[1].body: The emergency operation is documented minute by minute and corroborated by a full team. She is ruled out.
strings.folders[2].docs[2].title: Abu Walid Interview
strings.folders[2].docs[2].body: Hospital gates recorded no entry by him. The administrative ban remained in force.
strings.folders[3].name: Records
strings.folders[3].docs[0].title: Dispensing Signature Audit
strings.folders[3].docs[0].body: 11 forged dispensing signatures in the names of discharged patients — all during charge nurse Ramez's shifts.
strings.folders[3].docs[1].title: Access-Card Movement Log
strings.folders[3].docs[1].body: Ramez's card: on-call room at 04:10, then the service lift to the second floor at 04:16 — where the pen was found.
strings.folders[4].name: Confidential files
strings.folders[4].docs[0].title: The Report That Arrived Anyway
strings.folders[4].docs[0].body: Dr. Bassel's scheduled report reached management that morning, complete with names and figures. At the top of the list: the charge nurse.
strings.folders[4].docs[1].title: Confrontation Record
strings.folders[4].docs[1].body: Investigators confronted Ramez with the report and access-card log. He remained silent and requested a lawyer. He was referred for prosecution in custody.
strings.reports[0].title: The 04:10 Report
strings.reports[0].author: Investigation team
strings.reports[0].body: Two minutes in the room were enough to inject a sleeping man's shoulder. The subsequent route to the second-floor bin completes the instrument's timeline.
strings.reports[1].title: Motive Report
strings.reports[1].author: Assigned investigator
strings.reports[1].body: Murder to silence an auditor: the victim uncovered fraudulent dispensing, and the culprit killed to suppress a report... which the dead man delivered on schedule.
strings.notes[0].text: Report scheduled for 08:00 — the victim testified after death
strings.notes[1].text: Who goes down two floors to throw away a pen?
